To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

RDR6-dependent TAS1/TAS1c and TAS2 dsRNAs are processed from both ends by DCL4 in distinct registers to produce tasiRNAs and that a master siRNA produced from TAS1c controls a complex network that regulates TAS1/TAS gene expression.
the TAS1/TAS1/TAS2 network generates tasiRNAs from TAS1/TAS3/TAS2 transcripts, which are converted to dsRNas by RDR6, and the dsRNAs are processed by Dcl4 to tasiRNAs.
RDR6-mediated production of short dsRNAs from TAS1/TAS1a transcripts is initiated by miR173-directed cleavage and followed by a second cleavage guided by a TAS1a/TAS1c-derived siRNAs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the biogenesis, processing and regulation of plant tasiRNAs.
the biogenesis, function, and evolution of tasiRNAS.

the biogenesis of tasiRNPs (tasiRNA-containing RNP complexes) in Arabidopsis thaliana. tasiRNPs are a class of small RNA-containing RNP complexes that are produced from a subset of plant microRNA (miRNA) precursors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
RDR6-mediated dsRNA production is a general feature of plant siRNA production.
the RDR6-dependent dsRNAs are the major source of tasiRNAS in Arabidopsis.
tasiRNAs are generated in an RDR6-dependent, miRNA-directed, and DCL4-dependent manner.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the RDR6-dependent TAS1/TAS1/TAS1c/TAS2 network produces a variety of siRNAs that are processed from both ends of TAS1/Tas2 dsRNAs, some of which target the same transcripts to generate feedback regulation.
tasiRNA biogenesis and function is much more complicated than previously thought.
RDR6-mediated dsRNA formation is a general feature in siRNA biogenesis in plants.
The main takeaway from our work is that
RDR6-mediated dsRNA biogenesis is a general mechanism to produce siRNAs from transcripts that are cleaved by miRNAs and that the resulting tasiRNAs can regulate their own biogenesis.
the TAS gene network generates a complex network of siRNAs that regulate the expression of the TAS genes and their own biogenesis.
RDR6-dependent dsRNA biogenesis is more complex than previously thought and is involved in a variety of siRNA biogenesis pathways.
